title: What If a Magnitude 9 Quake Hit the Pacific Northwest?

scenes.text: What if the fault off the Pacific Northwest snapped? The ground is not the biggest danger.
The Cascadia fault runs about 600 miles. A magnitude 9 quake would throw people to the ground.
On the outer coast, the first tsunami arrives within minutes. Warning time: roughly ten to twenty.
Waves could travel over 40 miles an hour, and flood the outer coast 20 to 60 feet deep.
More waves can follow for up to twelve hours, so people must stay on high ground.
A ShakeAlert network could add minutes of notice. Minutes are the difference.

description:
